jobs.prompt:
chore: make the native gateway branch C++ only (no TypeScript, Rust or Bun anywhere)

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-gemini-merge-20261119-44556239421-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: the native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`), `static/` web assets, and some leftover tooling. 453 C++ test binaries (5,258 cases) pass in release and under sanitizers. OWNER DECISION: the delivered branch contains C++ code and C++ tests only; nothing in it, in its CI or in its packaging may need TypeScript, Bun, Node, Rust or Cargo, and no compute may be spent running any of those. If the TypeScript gateway is ever needed for comparison, the owner goes back to an earlier commit. Do NOT install or run Bun, Node, Deno, Rust or Cargo in this job, not even to "check" something: reason from the source. Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body: plain language, short (what was removed, what the repository contains now, how to build/test/package, what was verified, anything the gateway lost).

OWNER POLICY (binding): the gateway's behaviour and security must not change; less code is preferred.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- This task edits root files, `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-*.yml`, `.githooks/` and `cpp/gateway/**` as described. Do not delete or weaken C++ tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes.


HARD WORKING RULE: your process WILL be restarted without warning (model connections drop about every 15-30 minutes today) and then knows only what is committed. Commit after every small step; keep a checklist in your report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-cpp-only-ds-20261119.md` and tick it in the same commit. After a restart read the report and `git log` first. NEVER start a command that runs longer than about 10 minutes in the foreground: run one test binary or one small group at a time. Do NOT run full four-shard suites yourself: the repository's hosted CI runs the complete release, sanitizer and fuzz matrix automatically when your branch is pushed.

TASK
STEP A (first, as its own commits; write the resulting commit hash into the report under the heading "STATE A"): `git fetch origin agent-jobs/cppgw-residuals-1-20261119-44477130790-1` and merge it with an ordinary merge commit (no conflicts expected). Then `git revert --no-edit d35a8a8bbc9a986bded5bba2d9c0f0f1a11c4ea1` (it rejected unknown chat roles and Responses tool types through hard-coded allowlists; the owner chose to keep forwarding them like production). After the revert the oversized-`model` length checks from commit `b58afd3d1` must still be in `src/chat/envelope.cpp` and `src/responses_request.cpp` (re-add them if the revert took them), there is no role or tool-type allowlist, and that commit's allowlist-only tests are gone while all other tests remain. Build and run the tests that link those two files.

STEP B (C++ only). Inventory first, by `git ls-files` and `git grep`, everything that is or needs TypeScript/JavaScript/Bun/Node/Rust/Cargo, then remove it:
- The paired comparison against the TypeScript gateway: `cpp/gateway/conformance/` (runner, oracle scripts, pins), `cpp/gateway/tests/production_smoke/bun.ts` and `bunfig.toml`, the Bun/Node oracle paths of `cpp/gateway/bench/**` (keep benchmarks that run only the native gateway; delete Bun-only ones such as `bench/paths/json.ts`), `tests/helpers/*.mjs` if any remain, and every document section that tells the reader to run them (replace with one sentence: the comparison lives at the previous commit, hash from STATE A). Recorded fixture data that C++ tests replay (`*.inc` vectors, JSON fixtures) STAYS: it is C++ test input.
- Formatting toolchain: root `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `.prettierrc`, `.prettierignore`, the Prettier step of `.githooks/pre-commit` (keep a whitespace check with plain git if the hook has one, else delete the hook), and the "Format changed files" job or step in `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-ci.yml`. If the tree has `.clang-format`, a C++ format check may stay only if it needs no Bun/Node.
- The remaining `.ts` files: `cpp/gateway/packaging/native-kv/build-native-kv.ts` and `cpp/gateway/runtime/legacy-codec/typed-value.ts`. DECIDE BY EVIDENCE what they are for: read `cpp/gateway/packaging/**`, `cpp/gateway/tools/package.py`, `src/storage/native_addon.cpp`, `src/runtime/native_kv_bootstrap.cpp`, `src/rt/kv*.cpp`, `src/kv_conversion/**`, `runtime/startup.cpp`, `docs/RUNTIME.md`, `docs/rt/kv-durable.md` and the tests. The questions: (1) does the running gateway load `native-kv.node` (a Rust-built Node-API addon) or `linux-arm64.node` (confinement helper) at run time, or does the C++ code implement storage (`kv_sqlite.cpp`) and confinement (`permissions_linux.cpp`) itself and only verify/ship those files for parity proofs or offline tools? (2) is `typed-value.ts` executed by anything the gateway needs in production (it looks like an offline V8 value codec for a one-time data conversion)? Then: if the gateway does NOT need them at run time, remove the addons, their Rust/Cargo/Node build recipes (`packaging/portable/native.sh`, Rust toolchain download, `native-receipt.py`, licences that only covered them), the manifest/startup checks that demand them, and the tests that only test them, so the portable package is the C++ executables plus `static/` plus licences; keep startup's integrity checks for what remains. If the gateway DOES need one at run time (cannot open the production store or cannot confine itself without it), do NOT remove that one: say exactly why in the report and final message, keep its build recipe, and still remove everything else. Never weaken confinement and never change the on-disk data format the gateway reads and writes.
- CI: `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-ci.yml` and `cpp-gateway-release.yml` must not install or run Bun, Node (beyond what GitHub's own checkout/upload actions use internally), Rust or Cargo; `actionlint` them if it is installed (it is a Go binary; installing it is fine).
- Root documents: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore` describe a C++-only repository.
STEP C. Add `cpp/gateway/docs/CUTOVER.md`: a short checklist for the owner's week of real-world testing and later switch on an Arch Linux ARM host: build or download the package, verify the checksum, install side by side on another port with `EnvironmentFile=` (no implicit `.env`), point it at a COPY of the data first, health checks, switch, rollback. Use `docs/SIDE-BY-SIDE.md`, `docs/RELEASES.md` and `cpp/gateway/ops/` rather than inventing steps; mark anything you could not verify as UNVERIFIED. Put ONE table of every `UOS_GATEWAY_*` environment switch the code reads (grep for them) with default and effect into `docs/RUNTIME.md`.
VERIFICATION (small steps): `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py --check`; `git ls-files | grep -E '\.(ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs|rs)$|Cargo|package\.json|bun\.lock|bunfig'` prints nothing except files under `static/` (browser JavaScript served by the gateway stays) and vendored third-party sources if any; `git grep -nE '\b(bun|cargo|rustc|npm|node) ' -- .github cpp/gateway/packaging cpp/gateway/tools cpp/gateway/cmake` shows no command invocation; build the gateway executable and run the startup, static-file, KV, permissions and package-related tests in release, plus the tests of anything you edited; if you changed packaging, run the package build once (`cpp/gateway/packaging/portable/build.sh`, Docker is available) and its verifier, each as a background command you poll, not a foreground wait.

DONE WHEN
STATE A is recorded; the tree, CI and packaging are C++ only as defined (or the one exception is justified by evidence); CUTOVER.md and the switch table exist; the verification list passes; the report's checklist is fully ticked or the unticked items are explained.
